value: best sensitivity: lowest threshold 18 dB re 20 µPa rms at 2 kHz
method: behavioural audiogram: psychophysics by the method of constants with pure tones in an acoustic chamber; thresholds at the stimulus level giving a hit rate halfway between the false-alarm rate and 100%
conditions: a single bird, a male 6-year-old wild-caught great cormorant housed in captivity in an outdoor aviary at Kerteminde, Denmark; tested inside a 2.5×1×1 m acoustic chamber; 50 sessions performed, 5 excluded for false-alarm rates above 35%, used sessions 20-31% false alarms; the Abstract gives five frequencies but the Results refer to six frequencies and the other thresholds are only in Table 1 (an image, not read); ambient noise 27-76 dB below threshold, but the threshold-to-noise ratio was comparable to the estimated critical ratio at 2 kHz, where the authors state there is a slight risk the threshold was masked by ambient noise in some trials; thresholds by signal detection theory within 2 dB of the classical ones; the Discussion places the best sensitivity in the region of 1 to 2 kHz

source.authors: Maxwell A, Hansen KA, Ortiz ST, Larsen ON, Siebert U, Wahlberg M
source.title: In-air hearing of the great cormorant (Phalacrocorax carbo)
